sections.html:
The quickest sales here start with a decision: an agent listing or a direct sale to a cash buyer. Make it early, and settle permit and title questions before the first offer arrives. Buyers in a lakeside, retiree-heavy city have different expectations than buyers in a typical Arizona suburb.

The population was 57,144 in 2020 and is estimated at 59,358 on July 1, 2025. Households average 2.04 people, 73.2 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and residents 65 and over are 35.2 percent of the total. The median owner-occupied home is worth $455,400, median gross rent is $1,320, and the median household income is $70,148. The city sits on the east side of Lake Havasu, and Arizona State Route 95 is the only surface access.

Collect these documents before you list:

  • The recorded deed and parcel number
  • Mortgage and lien payoff statements
  • Permit records for pools, patio covers, additions and solar
  • Any vacation rental business license, if guests have stayed in the house
  • The latest Mohave County tax bill

Few Arizona towns are hotter, so a buyer checks the cooling system first. Summer days routinely reach 110 degrees, temperatures can pass 100 as early as April and as late as October, and July and August nights often stay between 80 and 90 degrees. Rainfall averages only about 4.16 inches a year, and winter highs run in the 60s and 70s. Dry air and strong sun punish roofing, exterior paint, window seals and pool equipment.

Because lots here have been sold since the 1960s, some houses are decades old. A folder of records answers a buyer's questions about wiring, plumbing and roofs:

  • Service receipts for the air conditioner and any recent replacement
  • The age and type of the roof covering, with any repairs
  • Photographs of pool plaster, pumps and fencing
  • Electric and water bills for the hottest months, since buyers ask about summer costs

These records help a buyer judge risk, and they back up your asking price if an offer arrives lower than you hoped.

The city's Building Permits page lists the jobs that need a permit: room additions, patio covers, detached structures over 200 square feet, swimming pools and spas, gas lines, electrical panel change-outs, rewires, photovoltaic systems, fireplace installations, wall removal and added or relocated plumbing fixtures. Retaining walls over 2 feet 6 inches on a slope, or 3 feet on level ground, also need one.

Smaller jobs do not. Painting, floor covering, minor drywall repair, replacing roof covering, replacing an existing water heater and replacing an existing air conditioner without increasing its weight, capacity, location or ampacity all go without a permit. If you find an unpermitted pool or addition in your own history, email Development Services for permit records on the address, or call 928-453-4148 and ask for the building group.

Permit typeReview time
Single-family home or duplex30 business days
Residential addition, garage or patio cover20 business days
Pools, retaining walls, mechanical, electrical and plumbing10 business days
Repeat review of residential plans5 business days

Those times matter if a buyer asks you to close an open permit before closing.

sections.h2: Code enforcement items that trip up sellers
sections.html: Code Enforcement pays attention to unscreened unlicensed vehicles, trash or debris visible from the street, structures in setback areas, and living in an RV or travel trailer for more than 7 days per calendar quarter on an improved residential lot. Clear any open complaint before listing. Trash cans may go to the curb no more than 12 hours before pickup.

A buyer can run a vacation rental here, but needs a local business license. The development code lists a vacation rental dwelling in its permitted uses table and requires the operator to hold a valid local business license.

State law caps what the city may do. Under A.R.S. 9-500.39 a city or town may not prohibit short-term rentals, may charge a permit fee of no more than the actual cost or $250, whichever is less, and may require owners to give neighbors notice, provide emergency contact information and carry at least $500,000 of liability insurance. A first verified violation can bring a penalty of up to $500 or one night's advertised rent, whichever is greater.

If you rented the house by the night, give buyers the license number, tax registration and insurance details. If you did not, say that plainly. For the current permit fee or ordinance requirement, call the city's licensing office, since fees change.

The Mohave County Treasurer bills property tax in two installments. The first half is due October 1 and becomes past due after 5:00 p.m. on November 1, or the next business day when November 1 is a weekend. The second half is due March 1 and past due after May 1, which falls on a Saturday in 2027, so it moves to May 3, 2027. Bills over $100 paid in full by December 31 owe no interest accrued after November 1, and late payments accrue 16 percent annually, prorated monthly.

The Treasurer has a payment drop box at the county building, 2001 College Drive, Suite 93. Use a sealed envelope with the payment stub and a check or money order payable to the Mohave County Treasurer, and no cash. Confirm with your escrow officer how the tax year will be split at closing.

Lake Havasu City has its own Mohave County Recorder office at the same address, open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. with a lunch closure from 12 to 1, phone (928) 453-0702 ext. 3021. The county lists a $30 recording fee, subject to A.R.S. 11-480. Every sale needs a completed Affidavit of Property Value or an exemption number on the deed under A.R.S. 11-1133.

Lake Havasu Unified School District No. 1 serves the city, with six elementary schools, one middle school and one high school. Names include Jamaica, Starline, Smoketree, Nautilus and Havasupai elementary schools, Oro Grande Classical Academy, Thunderbolt Middle School and Lake Havasu High School. Buyers with children will ask which school a home feeds, so look up the attendance information with the district before you list.

sections.h2: Closing on a Lake Havasu City house
sections.html: After you accept an offer, escrow opens with a title company. The officer searches for liens, gets your payoff statements, divides the year's property tax and prepares the deed and affidavit for recording. A cash purchase has no lender review, so the pace depends on title work and permits. If a buyer's inspector finds an unpermitted pool or addition, expect a request to close the permit, lower the price or accept the house as is. Decide your answer ahead of time, using the permit records you gathered.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lake Havasu City house that has unpermitted work?
faqs.a: Yes, but expect questions. Buyers' inspectors and lenders may ask for permit history on pools, additions and patio covers. Email Development Services for records on your address or call 928-453-4148, and decide whether to close the permit, price the repair, or sell to a buyer who accepts the house as is.

faqs.q: How hot is Lake Havasu City, and does it matter when I sell?
faqs.a: Very hot. Summer days regularly reach 110 degrees, and the state's record of 128 degrees Fahrenheit was set here. Buyers focus on the air conditioner, roof and pool equipment, so service records help your price hold up.

faqs.q: Does Lake Havasu City allow vacation rentals?
faqs.a: Yes. The development code lists a vacation rental dwelling in its permitted uses table and requires the operator to have a valid local business license. State law also bars a city from prohibiting short-term rentals, though it may require a permit and neighbor notice.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Lake Havasu City?
faqs.a: At the Mohave County Recorder office at 2001 College Drive, Suite 93, or at the main office in Kingman. The county lists a $30 fee, and the deed needs an Affidavit of Property Value or an exemption number. Your title company usually handles this for you at closing.

faqs.q: When is the next Mohave County property tax payment due?
faqs.a: The second half of 2026 taxes is due March 1, 2027 and becomes past due after 5 p.m. on May 3, 2027, because May 1 falls on a Saturday. Paying both halves in one payment by December 31, 2026 removes interest that accrued after November 1.
